chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
"It is disliked for a man to respond with the Talbiyah when he is called while he is in ihram."

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man addressed by the ruling
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ: with the talbiyah, the ritual invocation of hajj and ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.نُودِيَ: he is called or addressed by someone
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: is considered disliked in legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to respond with the talbiyah when someone calls a person in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal discouragement concerning the etiquette of one in ihram. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches that answering a caller with the talbiyah in that circumstance is makruh, indicating a disliked act within the rites of hajj.
